title: Examination of the peripheral auditory system using auditory evoked potentials following cochlear implantation
summary: Electroencephalography of the brainstem (eBERA) is used to assess auditory nerve conduction following cochlear implant (CI) surgery. This study investigates how the auditory nerve responds to different signals presented at various locations within the cochlea. The specific goal is to gain a better understanding of the temporal processing of different signals on the auditory nerves.

interventions.name: Recording of eBERA responses in subjects with cochlear implants, followed by the determination of the latencies of auditory nerve responses waves I–V.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
A cochlear implant must have been in use for at least 6 months
Speech recognition with a cochlear implant in a free-field setting of at least 30% word recognition
Cochlear implant (CI) fitting using implants from Cochlear and MED-EL
Exclusion criteria:
Short duration of cochlear implant use
Individuals with known neural hearing loss
Other pre-existing neurological conditions
Other severe comorbidities that would complicate the trial
